title: India Finishes Fourth at CWG 2026 With 39 Medals as Boxers Lead Historic Gold Rush
excerpt: Seven boxing golds headlined India’s 39-medal haul at Glasgow, where Mirabai Chanu made history with her third successive gold.
body:
• India won 39 medals (13 gold, 17 silver, 9 bronze) to finish fourth at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.
  • Boxing delivered a record-breaking seven golds and ten medals total — the most by any nation in the sport at a single CWG.
  • Weightlifter Mirabai Chanu became only the second Indian athlete to win three consecutive Commonwealth Games gold medals.
  • India recorded firsts in judo (two golds) and decathlon (Tejaswin Shankar’s maiden medal), while para athletes delivered their best-ever showing.

Boxing Powers India’s Best Event Showing

The Commonwealth Games 2026 in Glasgow wrapped up on August 2 with India claiming fourth place behind Australia (171 medals), England (110), and Canada (63). The 122-member Indian contingent competed across ten sports, but it was the boxing ring that proved most productive.

Indian boxers dominated the competition with seven gold and three silver medals — ten medals in total. No nation in Commonwealth Games history has won more boxing medals at a single edition. The gold rush included standout performances across weight categories, with Jaismine Lamboria earning the honour of carrying India’s flag at the closing ceremony.

“The performance of our athletes has made 140 crore Indians proud. Their dedication, discipline, and determination are truly inspiring.”

— Prime Minister Narendra Modi, congratulating the Indian contingent

Chanu Makes History, Again

Weightlifter Mirabai Chanu set the tone early, winning gold in the women’s 48kg category. The Manipuri lifter became the first Indian female athlete to win medals at four successive Commonwealth Games and only the second Indian overall to claim three consecutive golds. She also served as India’s flag bearer at the opening ceremony.

Weightlifting contributed several more medals to India’s tally, with Rishikanta Singh Chanambam, Muthupandi Raja, Gyaneshwari Yadav, and Valluri Ajaya Babu all winning silver medals in their respective categories. Bindyarani Devi and Harjinder Kaur added further podium finishes.

Historic Firsts in Judo, Decathlon, and Track

India’s judo team achieved a breakthrough at Glasgow, winning three medals including two golds — the country’s first-ever Commonwealth Games gold medals in the sport. Asmita Dey and Harsh Singh scripted history with their victories.

In athletics, Gulveer Singh became the first Indian track and field athlete to win two individual medals at a single Commonwealth Games, claiming silver and bronze. Tejaswin Shankar won India’s maiden CWG decathlon medal. Neeraj Chopra, the Olympic javelin champion, settled for silver after Sri Lanka’s Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage produced the winning throw.

Para Athletes Shine

Indian para athletes delivered their best-ever performance at a single Commonwealth Games, winning seven medals including three golds. The showing underscored the growing depth of India’s para-sport programmes, with Sharmila winning gold in the women’s shot put F57 category.

Where India Stands in the CWG Pecking Order

India’s 39-medal haul represents a decline from the 60 medals won at Birmingham 2022, though the absence of shooting — historically India’s strongest CWG discipline — from the Glasgow programme partly explains the drop. Wrestling, another traditional Indian strength, was also reduced in scope.

Australia dominated proceedings with 70 golds and 171 total medals. Scotland, as host nation, finished fifth with 39 medals but fewer golds than India, which held fourth on gold count. The 2030 edition is expected to bring back several disciplines that favour India’s medal prospects.
nri_angle: Strong performances by Indian athletes at Glasgow provide a point of pride for the global diaspora and spotlight India’s growing sports infrastructure.
